questions.question: Minutes after an IV antibiotic begins, a client develops wheezing, lip swelling, vomiting, and hypotension. What is the priority action?
choices: Stop the infusion, activate emergency response, and initiate the anaphylaxis protocol
Wait for hives before intervening
Slow the infusion and document later
Give an oral antihistamine as the only treatment
questions.explanation: The respiratory and circulatory findings indicate anaphylaxis even if hives are absent. Stop exposure and initiate emergency airway, breathing, circulation, and first-line epinephrine treatment per protocol.

questions.question: A client reports nausea after codeine but denies rash, swelling, wheezing, or hypotension. How should the RN document this history?
choices: Record codeine, nausea, timing, severity, and outcome as a possible intolerance
Document anaphylaxis without further detail
Remove the reaction because nausea never matters
Record only “allergy unknown”
questions.explanation: Precise reaction documentation distinguishes a likely predictable intolerance from immune-mediated allergy while preserving clinically useful information.

questions.question: Which finding after starting a new medication requires the most urgent escalation?
choices: Painful blistering rash with oral and eye erosions
Mild dry mouth without other symptoms
Transient metallic taste
One episode of mild nausea after food
questions.explanation: Painful blistering with mucosal involvement may indicate Stevens–Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis and requires immediate drug and emergency evaluation.

questions.question: Which combination is an example of pharmacodynamic stacking?
choices: An opioid, benzodiazepine, and alcohol producing additive respiratory depression
One drug increasing another drug's renal clearance
A tablet dissolving more slowly with food
A medication being dispensed under its generic name
questions.explanation: Different CNS depressants can add to sedation and ventilatory suppression without necessarily changing one another's blood concentrations.

questions.question: Which approach best creates a reliable admission medication history?
choices: Ask what is actually taken and compare several sources such as bottles, pharmacy fills, records, and caregiver information
Copy the oldest medication list without interviewing the client
Record prescription tablets but exclude drops, inhalers, and supplements
Assume a pharmacy fill proves the client takes every dose
questions.explanation: A best possible history uses a detailed interview and multiple sources because no single list or fill record proves the actual regimen.

questions.question: During discharge reconciliation, a home beta blocker is absent from the new list and no reason is documented. What should the RN do?
choices: Clarify whether the omission is intentional before discharge
Add it independently to the prescription list
Tell the client to choose whether to restart it
Ignore it because only newly prescribed drugs matter
questions.explanation: The discrepancy must be classified as intentional and documented or unintentional and resolved with an authorized prescriber. Abrupt beta-blocker interruption may also cause rebound harm.

questions.question: A client takes two combination cold products and acetaminophen for pain. What is the RN's priority concern?
choices: Duplicate active ingredients may cause an unrecognized overdose
OTC products cannot interact with prescriptions
Different brand names guarantee different ingredients
Acetaminophen has no dose-related toxicity
questions.explanation: Combination products can contain the same active ingredient. Total exposure from prescription and OTC sources must be calculated to prevent toxicity.

questions.question: After a medication error reaches a client, which action is appropriate?
choices: Assess and treat the client, notify the appropriate clinicians, document clinical facts, and complete the safety report per policy
Hide the event if no harm is immediately visible
Place the confidential incident-report narrative in the progress note
Delay assessment until a manager determines fault
questions.explanation: Client assessment and treatment come first. Objective care is documented in the clinical record, while the separate safety process supports system learning rather than blame.

questions.question: Which finding best demonstrates effective discharge medication reconciliation?
choices: The client explains what was started, stopped, changed, and continued and has a feasible follow-up plan
The printed list contains every historical prescription
The client agrees without reviewing the instructions
All home medications were automatically resumed
questions.explanation: Teach-back of the final changes plus access, monitoring, and follow-up shows that the reconciled plan is both accurate and usable.

questions.question: A serious unexpected adverse reaction has been stabilized. Which statement about FDA MedWatch reporting is correct?
choices: Follow organizational policy; a report can be useful even when causality is not proven
A report is allowed only after absolute proof of causation
External reporting replaces clinical documentation
Reporting should occur before emergency treatment
questions.explanation: Urgent care and clinical documentation come first. MedWatch can receive serious adverse-event and product-problem reports without definitive proof that the product caused the event.
